newsitem.title: USA: Plaintiff airlines to appeal Miami rate ruling.
newsitem.headline: Plaintiff airlines to appeal Miami rate ruling.

text.p: The six airlines that challenged the funding for American Airlines' new terminal at Miami International Airport will appeal a federal ruling that found the rate strucuture fair, the plaintiffs' attorney said.
Attorney Barry Davidson said Thursday the carriers "absolutely" would appeal to the Federal Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia within 30 days.
"This is hardly the end of the trail," Davidson told Reuters.
The U.S. Department of Transportation ruled Wednesday the airport's plan to require its 92 passenger airlines to share the cost of American's new $975 million terminal was fair and reasonable.
American, a unit of AMR Corp, said it was prepared to meet the appeal.
"We can't imagine on what basis they would appeal, since the DOT was quite emphatic on these issues," American spokesman Al Becker said.
